input.content: Pattern: idempotency/recovery key silently narrowed. In an idempotent save-with-recovery function, the dedup lookup was changed from a keyed get on the idempotency key (operation_id, the dict key) to a linear scan matching a coarser attribute (workspace). Consequences to watch for whenever a lookup key changes: (1) Lost update — once ANY record exists for the coarser key, subsequent calls take the "found" branch and apply the stored record's values, silently dropping the caller's freshly-passed values while still returning success. (2) Response/state inconsistency — the function returns the caller's operation_id but the persisted record carries a different operation_id and is never stored under the new key. (3) O(1) keyed lookup degrades to O(n) scan over an unbounded dict. Review rule: when an idempotency/dedup key is broadened or an apply becomes conditional (e.g. `if status == "pending"`), trace what happens to a NEW request that matches an EXISTING record — confirm the new inputs are not silently discarded.
